MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 6, 2024

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli,
  Schachter, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, APRIL 1, 2024

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton clarified that
the additional conditions of approval were included in the motion and added to the final
resolution.

VICE CHAIR OLSON, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF APRIL 1, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

Michelle Mathis, 10 Dapplegray Lane, commented on the project approved on April 1, 2024 at 12
Sorrel Lane and stated that the rear fence encroaches into the bridle trail easement and causes
a hardship to provide for trash and fire services. Ms. Mathis stated that she had contacted
Commissioner Schachter, not realizing that he was on the Planning Commission, and was
referred to another attorney. She stated that in 2020 the City was notified and was unaware that
this issue existed; however, the applicant recently did their own survey and found that the fence
is encroaching into the bridle trail easement. Ms. Mathis further explained the hardships that this
is causing and stated that the applicant does not believe that the fence is encroaching in the
easement; she would like to make sure that this issue is addressed.

Director Naughton stated that the appeal period for this item has expired; however, staff can
discuss this issue with Ms. Mathis.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER YOO, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

 MINUTES, MAY 6, 2024
  1
 7.  PUBLIC HEARING

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240158; ADDRESS: 550 Deep Valley Drive, Rolling
  Hills Estates, CA 90274 / 550 Deep Valley Drive, Unit 127, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274;
  APPLICANT: CYP LLC / Multiverse Platforms Inc; A request to amend the Master
  Conditional Use Permit for the Promenade on the Peninsula (CUP-240159) to increase
  the maximum allowable restaurant use (including alcohol sales) from 15% to 30% of the
  gross leasable area and a request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240160) to allow a
  26,193 square foot bowling alley with ancillary restaurant use (including alcohol sales)
  within the Promenade on the Peninsula.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe presented Planning Application No. PA-240158 summarizing the staff
report. The first applicant (CYP LLC) is requesting to amend the existing Master Conditional Use
Permit, which allows for 15% of leasable space for restaurant use, including alcohol sales, to a
maximum of 30%. The CUP findings criteria are met. In addition, parking is sufficient for the added
restaurant use and the exterior noise standards were explained.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that the second applicant (Multiverse Platforms Inc) proposes
to operate a bowling alley with ancillary restaurant use, including alcohol sales. Details on the
operation of the business were provided. In addition to the bowling alley and restaurant; there will
be a “family fun zone”, which will offer a variety of arcade games. Currently, there are restrictions
on arcade use; however, with the upcoming zoning changes arcades will be allowed with a CUP.
The applicants will apply for a CUP prior to the start of business. The CUP findings criteria are
met. The existing parking will accommodate this use and the noise standards were explained.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission,
open the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing;
and, adopt Resolution No. PA-240158a, approving an amendment to the Master Conditional
Use Permit to increase the allowable restaurant with on-premise alcohol sales from 15% to
30% of GLA for Promenade on the Peninsula; and Resolution No. PA-240158b, approving a
Conditional Use Permit for a bowling alley with ancillary restaurant use, including on-premise
alcohol sales, and both applications are in accordance with the California Environmental
Quality Act (Public Resources Code §21000 et seq.: “CEQA”), and determined that the
projects are Categorically Exempt under Class 1, Section 15301 – Existing Facilities.

Director Naughton clarified that prior to posting the agenda, the resolution numbers were
changed to their respective CUP numbers, which are Resolution No. CUP-240159 for the
Master CUP and Resolution No. CUP-240160 for the bowling alley CUP.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

Cynthia Hu, CYP LLC, provided a statement regarding her background with growing up in
Rolling Hills Estates and how meaningful the mall is to her and her family. She stated that the
mall has deteriorated over the years and shared the purpose and the vision that they have
for the mall and her hope is that the needs and wants of the community are consistent with
their vision of restaurants and family-friendly activities. Ms. Hu also shared that she wants to
bring back a sense of community and shared that tenants are required to participate in mall
events.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI expressed his concern with the requirements for smaller versus
major tenants. Ms. Hu explained that the mall has a high vacancy rate at the moment and the
increase to 30% would likely be taken from office and unused retail space. She further explained
that the smaller tenants would not need to apply for a separate CUP and this would be counted
in the Master CUP allowance; however, all major tenants (which includes tenant spaces of 10,000
SF or more) would need to apply for a separate CUP.

CHAIR MEDAWAR expressed that he is excited that a local family purchased the mall and is glad
to see these projects coming before the commission.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN expressed her appreciation for Ms. Hu and her family for
stepping up to give this very large portion of the commercial district some much needed attention.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about who would be operating the blowing alley

 and about security. Ms. Hu stated that the actual tenants are present and explained the security
updates that have been made to the mall. She stated that there have been no significant issues
at the mall in quite some time since the security updates have been put in place.

COMMSSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if there are any conditions of approval in regard to
security in the prior MCUP. Director Naughton stated that there were not; however, the
Commission may add this condition of approval. COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN added
that a security plan should be submitted to the City for review and approval in consultation with
the Sheriff’s Department.

Ms. Hu further explained that she does not believe that she could have a successful environment
unless it is secure.

CHAIR MEDAWAR suggested that the owner meet with the new Sheriff’s Captain and coordinate
having some presence at the mall, to have direct communication with either a radio or direct line
to the Sheriff’s Department.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked about the parking lot repairs. Ms. Hu stated that the parking lot on the
4th level is open. The parking lot structural repair is 90% complete.

VICE CHAIR OLSON stated that he is also looking forward to this project. He inquired about
arrangements made with the Norris Theatre for parking when they are holding special events.
Director Naughton stated that this was settled through the courts resulting in an enhanced
agreement for additional parking, which was added to the original agreement.

VICE CHAIR OLSON expressed his concern with the aspect of younger people and alcohol
consumption and asked if there were any plans in place to control any issues that may arise. Ms.
Hu stated that on the primary level (1st floor) there will be quick and grab restaurants without the
full alcohol licenses. The sit-down restaurants will have full alcohol licenses. Director Naughton
further explained how the CUP licenses will work with the different uses within the mall.

A brief discussion ensued on the Master CUP and major tenants, who would still require a
separate CUP.

Krista Hu, CYP LLC, commented that she would like a place where she can have food or drink
with a friend and her kids can have a place for activities. She also stated that the security cameras
are constantly being monitored and they are alerted when an unusual activity occurs.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked about the number of security personnel. Ms. Hu stated that there are
three now and more are brought in during special events.

Raman Walia, Applicant, thanked the commission and stated that they are excited to bring this
proposal and vision to the City. He stated that he has two children, one in elementary and one in
high school. He stated that he understands the responsibility of bringing this kind of facility to the
City and stated that they plan to have sophisticated security cameras across the entire facility.
Mr. Walia further spoke about bringing family-friendly entertainment center to the community. He
also addressed the importance of having a secure place that family and friends can enjoy.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Mr. Walia shared that this
will be his first time operating this type of business; however, he stated that he has previous
experience with various organizations and understands what it takes to provide different
entertainment concepts to customers. He stated that he and his partner Raj bring a lot of business
and management experience and added that they are working with industry leaders who have
done similar projects many times before.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked how long it will take for the project to be complete.
Mr. Walia estimated that from this point, the project should take approximately nine to twelve
months to complete.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the drop-off and pick-up location and the impact to
traffic. Mr. Walia stated that they will be taking portions of four units and will need to consult with
the property owners on drop-off locations. CHAIR MEDAWAR encouraged that this be looked at
as part of the plans.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 6, 2024
  3
 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PA-240158 AND APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. CUP-240159 AND
  RESOLUTION NO. CUP-240160.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN suggested an amendment to the motion to add a condition
of approval that the applicant shall prepare a security plan for the entire property subject to CUP-
240159 and shall be reviewed by the LA County Sheriff’s Department and approved by the
Community Development Director. The security plan shall be coordinated between the applicant
and all tenants on the property that have an alcohol license or otherwise require security.

There were no objections to the amended motion.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, YOO
NOES
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. CUP-
240159, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the city of Rolling Hills Estates granting an
amendment to the Master conditional use permit for the Promenade on the Peninsula to increase
the maximum allowable restaurant, this including alcohol sales from 15% to 30% of the gross
leasable area at 550 Deep Valley Drive; additionally, the Planning Commission has approved
Resolution No. CUP-240160, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
Estates granting an Conditional Use Permit for a 26,193 square foot bowling alley with ancillary
restaurant use including alcohol sales within the Promenade on the Peninsula at 550 Deep Valley
Dr. Unit 127. There is 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City Council,
by its own motion may appeal this project.

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

NONE

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI reminded the commission of the proposed special meeting for
May 21 or May 22. Director Naughton stated that this meeting will be held in order to present in
code form the changes to the zoning ordinance and then give the Planning Commission time to
review and discuss and work out any issues; the hope is to bring an ordinance to the June
Planning Commission meeting and make a recommendation to the City Council.

The Planning Commission agreed that the meeting will be adjourned to the Planning Commission
meeting on Tuesday, May 21, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, APRIL 9, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 8:08 p.m. to the next Adjourned Planning
Commission meeting on Tuesday, May 21, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber,
4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.
